Name: bindings_need_a_query_only_when_untestable
Title: A Query Is Needed Only for Untestable Bindings: Planted Scene-Level Procedure Bindings Separate Compiled Rules, Compiled Tables and Scene-Keyed Retrieval
Short Hypothesis: Instance-specific bindings make an inference-time per-instance lookup (a scene-keyed query over experience, or a reader-routed table compiled from it) necessary only when the binding cannot be probed before committing. Planting scene-level bindings in ALFWorld (which of two same-looking appliances heats/cools/cleans is fixed per kitchen and invisible in the observation) under two feedback regimes (testable: a wrong attempt returns 'Nothing happens' and can be retried; untestable: it returns the normal success string and silently spends the step) and scoring every arm by its swap penalty (success unswapped minus success swapped, paired within game) predicts an interaction: under testable a 60-token run-time-test rule removes the penalty as fully as scene-keyed retrieval at zero uncached prefill; under untestable the rule is inert by construction and the penalty is removed only by artifacts that carry the binding, by scene-keyed retrieval and by an observation-keyed compiled table equally. Hence the retrieval residual over the best static arm stays at the natural residual measured at q = 0 (+17.2) once the static artifact enumerates the bindings, and grows by the full penalty only when the artifact names a test and the environment gives no signal.
Related Work: On this node the retrieval gain is scene-independent (unseen ~ seen) because ALFWorld's object placements are per-instance and its procedures per-type; the brief asks that the property that would make a query necessary be manipulated, not named (Q2). SGR-Bench (2605.22219) shows search agents fail by establishing the wrong site-specific state and leaves untested whether stored site procedures or prior trajectories would fix it; Mem2ActBench (2601.19935) shows memory-grounded parameters are mishandled but does not separate retrieval from application; SWE-ContextBench (2602.08316) shows related-task experience helps only when correctly selected. 'When Agents Commit Too Soon' (2606.22936) diagnoses silent failures from premature commitment but does not manipulate whether a non-committing probe exists; the untestable regime here is exactly a silent one-shot commitment and the testable regime exactly a free probe. ICAL (2406.14596) and task-recognition-vs-task-learning (2305.09731) frame what demonstrations supply without a run-time-testability axis. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed overlap; abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (5.95) posited that abstraction loses bindings; here bindings are planted, the compiled table keeps them, the compiled rule recovers them by probing, and the feedback regime that decides between them is manipulated on the same games. Agent Workflow Memory-style induced workflows are the nearest compiled form; the searched literature returned no version of it with a run-time probe or a bindings manipulation.
Abstract: Whether an agent needs to query its experience at inference time or can use a prompt compiled once depends on whether the task carries bindings that only past experience reveals and that the agent cannot probe before committing. We manipulate both in ALFWorld. A text wrapper swaps, per kitchen, the names of the procedure-critical receptacle and a same-scene partner (microwave 1 <-> stoveburner 1 for heat; fridge 1 <-> cabinet 1 for cool; sinkbasin 1 <-> countertop 1 for clean), with a response-template map so the two look identical under every non-procedure action; two complementary swap assignments run every test game in both its swapped and its unswapped state, so each arm is scored by its within-game swap penalty. A second wrapper level sets the feedback regime for the procedure action on the wrong appliance: testable (the real 'Nothing happens'; retry allowed) or untestable (the normal success string; the step is silently spent and the failure surfaces at the goal check). The expert bank is re-rendered under each assignment and replay-validated; 200 procedure-type train games are held out of it as extra seen-kitchen test games (264 seen procedure games x 2 states x 2 seeds per arm). Arms share the best measured static base (static3, stale) and add: a 60-token run-time-test rule; a compiled ~30-row per-kitchen table keyed by the receptacle-count signature of the initial observation; per-game oracle names (compliance gate and ceiling); scene-keyed top-3 retrieval (initial observation + goal); oracle same-kitchen retrieval; whole-bank_80 with the same-kitchen item present or replaced, randomised within game; and type-agnostic playbook versions of the rule and table arms. Predictions: under testable the rule's swap penalty is <= 12 and within 12 of retrieval's; under untestable retrieval's and the table's penalties are <= 12 while the rule's equals the stale base's; the whole bank removes the penalty only when the same-kitchen item is present; the rule's probe costs 2-4 steps and fires only in swapped kitchens. The claim: bindings alone do not make a query necessary; untestable bindings make a per-instance lookup necessary, and a table keyed on the observation is as good a lookup as a query.
Experiments: Wrapper: regex renaming layer over TextWorld observations, goal text and actions (inverse map on actions), swapping per kitchen the names of the procedure-critical receptacle and a same-scene partner (microwave 1 <-> stoveburner 1 for heat; fridge 1 <-> cabinet 1 for cool; sinkbasin 1 <-> countertop 1 for clean), with a response-template map so each name shows its own normal strings under every non-procedure action (go to, open, close, examine, take, put); leak probe: a scripted sweep of all non-procedure actions on both members of each pair must return identical strings in swapped and unswapped kitchens before any cell runs. Binding levels: q = 0 (base environment) and q = .5 under two complementary assignments A and A-bar over the seen kitchens, so every game runs in both its swapped and its unswapped state and every kitchen is swapped exactly once. Feedback regime, applied only to the procedure action on the wrong appliance: testable = the real 'Nothing happens', retry allowed; untestable = the normal success string is returned and the procedure step is spent (later attempts on either appliance return the success string without effect; failure surfaces at the goal check). Bank: expert pool re-rendered under each assignment (text renaming of affected steps), every item replayed and kept only if it succeeds in its kitchen's swap state; 200 procedure-type train games held out of the bank as extra seen-kitchen test games. Test set: 64 procedure-type (heat/cool/clean) valid_seen games + 200 held-out train games = 264 seen procedure games; each arm runs them x 2 assignments x 2 seeds = 1056 episodes (528 swapped, 528 unswapped, paired within game and seed). Arms (S = static3, the best static arm of Measurement C, 3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars rendered at base names, i.e. stale, ~430 tokens cached; T = the type-agnostic six-procedure playbook, C's 400 tokens): S0 static3; S1 static3 + 60-token run-time-test rule ('use the named appliance; if the response is Nothing happens, go to its partner and do the step there'); S2 static3 + compiled per-kitchen table (~30 rows, ~900 tokens, cached; row key = receptacle-count signature of the initial observation, value = which name heats, cools and cleans, compiled by rule from the bank of the current assignment; signature uniqueness and (kitchen, type) coverage >= .9 checked mechanically before running); S3 static3-oracle (per game, the exemplars' appliance names replaced by the correct names for the test kitchen under the current assignment; identical to S0 in unswapped kitchens); T0 playbook + rule; T1 playbook + table; R3 scene-keyed retrieval k = 3 (query = initial observation + goal, embedding retriever over the bank of the current assignment; ~430 uncached tokens per episode; same-kitchen hit rate computed offline and pre-registered, >= .8 required or the key is strengthened with the receptacle-count string); R3o oracle-scene retrieval (the three same-kitchen same-type items forced); W+ / W- whole-bank_80 (type-balanced sample of 80 items from the current assignment's bank, fixed per seed, ~11k tokens, cached within episode; W+ puts the top same-kitchen same-type item into a random same-type slot, W- puts a random other-kitchen same-type item into the same slot; paired within game). Cells: untestable: S0, S1, S2, S3, T1, R3, R3o, W+, W- (9 arms); testable: S0, S1, S2, T0, R3 (5 arms); q = 0 (base environment, the standard 274 x 2 cell): S1, S2, R3 (k0, static3, k3 are already measured); wrapper controls: S0 and R3 under untestable on the 76 non-procedure valid_seen games x 2 assignments x 2 seeds (304 each). Count: 14 x 1056 + 3 x 548 + 2 x 304 = 17,036 episodes; at v1's throughput (~25 episodes/min over two vLLM replicas of Qwen3-32B, one per A100, 30-45 min per 948-episode arm) ~11.5 h wall with arms spread across both replicas, plus one day for the wrapper, bank re-rendering and the offline pre-checks. Cut from v1: goal-keyed k = 3 (its exposure to the wrong binding is .5 by construction), the permuted-table placebo (forced once the table routes: a routed wrong row is an actively wrong binding), k0 at q = .5 (a stale prior is the same floor as a stale exemplar), and all unseen-kitchen cells (every bank-derived arm is at floor there by construction under untestable, and the rule's bank-independence is a construction fact under testable). Steps and uncached prefill per episode logged. Order: leak probe, table coverage and hit rate offline; P1 gate (S3 vs S0 untestable); then S1, S2, R3 under each regime; then R3o, T0, T1, W+/W-, q = 0.
Baselines and Ablations: Baseline is the best static arm of Measurement C (static3, type-conditioned) and its compiled augmentations built from the same bank (S1 rule, S2 table), on the same (game, seed, assignment); every retrieval number is reported as R3 minus the best of S0/S1/S2 in that regime, with the raw residual on swapped games stated against the measured +17.2 natural residual. Type-agnostic controls T0/T1 (six-procedure playbook base) are run so that the run-time test and the table routing are shown on a prompt that does not select by type. S3 (per-game oracle names) is the compliance gate and the ceiling for any artifact that carries the binding; R3o separates retriever misses from reader non-use; W+/W- is the whole-bank long-context arm with the binding's presence randomised within game; rule vs table separates a run-time probe from enumeration; the two regimes separate probe-able from silent-commit failures on the same games; the swap penalty on pick-type games and the q = 0 arms check that the wrapper, the scene key and the added artifacts are harmless where no binding exists.
Falsifiable Predictions: Notation: D(arm, regime) = success(unswapped) - success(swapped) in points on the 264 seen procedure games, paired within (game, seed) via the complementary assignments (528 pairs; floor +-8); contrasts between arms are paired on the same (game, seed, assignment); margin 12 (~half the measured +24 procedure-type retrieval gain at q = 0, above the floor), 20 for gates; '<= 12' claims are declared only if the one-sided 95% upper bound is below 12, equivalence claims by TOST with the 90% CI inside [-12, +12]. Construction checks, reported not scored: D(S0, untestable) >= 20 (a stale exemplar fails in swapped kitchens; < 20 means a leak and the wrapper is fixed before any confirmatory cell); D(S1, untestable) within +-8 of D(S0, untestable) (the rule is inert without a signal); D on the 76 pick-type games within +-8 of 0 for S0 and R3; at q = 0, S1 and S2 within +-8 of static3 and R3 - static3 within +-8 of the measured k3 - static3 = +17.2 (scene key and artifacts harmless without bindings). P1 (compliance gate; untestable; arms S3 vs S0): D(S0) - D(S3) >= 20. Falsified if < 12: the reader keeps its prior over a named appliance, no compiled artifact can carry a binding, and the study stops. P2 (testable: a run-time test rule suffices; arms S1, S0, R3, T0): D(S1, testable) <= 12; D(S0, testable) - D(S1, testable) >= 12; TOST |D(R3, testable) - D(S1, testable)| <= 12; secondary D(T0, testable) <= 12. Falsified if D(S1, testable) >= 12 (the reader does not execute the probe and the penalty stays), or if D(S0, testable) < 12 (the reader recovers from 'Nothing happens' on its own, so the rule carries nothing; reported as 'testable bindings need no artifact'), or if D(R3, testable) is below D(S1, testable) by >= 12 (a query beats the probe even with informative feedback). P3 (headline; untestable: a scene-keyed query is needed over the rule and suffices; arms R3, S1, R3o): D(R3, untestable) <= 12, against D(S1, untestable) >= 20 (construction). Falsified if D(R3, untestable) >= 12: the reader does not transfer a retrieved same-kitchen trajectory's appliance name against its prior. Attribution: the same-kitchen hit rate of the scene key (pre-registered offline, >= .8 required) and R3o; if D(R3o) <= 12 but D(R3) >= 12 the null is the retriever's and the claim survives only for the oracle key; if D(R3o) >= 12 too, the headline is false. P3 is not implied by P1: S3 inserts the correct name into the exemplar the reader already follows; R3 must make the reader prefer a retrieved trajectory's name to its prior with no instruction that names are swapped. The interaction D(S1, untestable) - D(S1, testable) >= 20 versus D(R3, untestable) - D(R3, testable) <= 12 is the 'only when untestable' statement: its rule half is fixed by construction and reported, its retrieval half is P3 with P2. P4 (untestable: an observation-keyed table matches the query; arms S2, R3, T1): D(S2, untestable) <= 12 and TOST |D(R3, untestable) - D(S2, untestable)| <= 12; secondary D(T1, untestable) <= 12. Falsified if D(S2, untestable) >= 12: the reader cannot route a ~30-row observation-keyed table to its row, so enumerable bindings still need a query and the residual over the best static arm exceeds the natural residual by the routing failure. The raw residual R3 - S2 on swapped games is predicted to equal the natural residual (+17.2 overall, ~ +24 on procedure types, CI half-width ~ +-5), not zero; the manipulation that keeps the binding from adding to it is the table's enumeration, and P4 fails exactly when R3 - S2 on swapped games exceeds R3 - S2 on unswapped games by >= 12. P5 (testable: the probe is cheap and bounded; arms S1, S0 step logs): steps(S1, swapped) - steps(S1, unswapped), paired within game, lies in [2, 4] (one failed attempt plus one move); falsified if the 95% CI lower bound is >= 5 (the failed probe triggers exploration, so the test is not a cheap substitute for the query) or if steps(S1) - steps(S0) on unswapped games is >= 1 (the reader over-tests when the binding holds); the lower bound 2 is mechanical and is a check on P2, not a prediction. Uncached prefill (R3/R3o ~430 per episode; S1 0) is by construction and reported on the accuracy-cost plane. P6 (untestable: the whole bank carries the binding only if the reader can locate it; arms W+ vs W-): on swapped seen games W+ - W- >= 12, paired within game (528 pairs, floor +-8). Falsified if < 12: the reader cannot locate the same-kitchen item among 79 others, of which the same-type ones carry the opposite binding half the time, so long context does not substitute for a keyed lookup at this bank size. W+ - R3 is reported, not predicted.
Measurement and Noise Control: Primary estimand: the swap penalty D(arm, regime) = success(unswapped) - success(swapped) in points on the 264 seen procedure games, paired within (game, seed) through the complementary assignments: 528 pairs per arm, floor +-8 (the brief's 274 x 2 floor); contrasts between arms are paired on the same (game, seed, assignment). Margins 12 (~half the measured +24 procedure-type retrieval gain at q = 0, above the floor) and 20 for gates; equivalence by TOST with the 90% CI inside [-12, +12], a margin above the +-8 half-width so that an undetected difference at the floor cannot pass; bootstrap over games with seeds nested; permutation tests over games for each contrast. Complementary assignments mean every kitchen is swapped exactly once, so no kitchen-specific pattern can carry a result and no second assignment is needed. The 200 held-out train games are pre-registered as test games and excluded from the bank (analysed as a stratum if their q = 0 success differs from valid_seen by >= 12). Offline pre-checks: leak probe, signature uniqueness, table coverage (>= .9 of (kitchen, type) cells), R3 same-kitchen hit rate (>= .8). Construction checks reported, not scored: D(S0, untestable) >= 20; D(S1, untestable) within +-8 of D(S0, untestable); pick-type penalties within +-8 of 0; q = 0 arms within +-8 of static3 (S1, S2) and of the measured +17.2 residual (R3). P1 gates every confirmatory cell. Uncached prefill per episode (R3/R3o ~430 uncached; S and T arms cached; W+/W- ~11k, cached within episode, uncached across games) and steps per episode logged; every arm placed on the accuracy-cost plane. Pre-registration before the first confirmatory cell.

Risk Factors and Limitations: The compliance gate may fail (the reader keeps its prior over a named appliance); then the swap is implausible to this reader and the study stops rather than strengthening the wrapper. Name swaps are a stylised binding: the claim is about the existence of a cheap non-committing probe, a property of real environments (silent API or UI failures), not about renaming. The untestable regime bundles undetectability with irreversibility because an undetectable-but-reversible failure is probe-able by redundancy (a 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' rule needs no binding); that third regime is a stated limit of the contrast and is not run. Contents of the swapped receptacles are not rewritten (a fridge full of plates is a weak leak); the construction check on D(S0, untestable) bounds it. Table routing depends on the receptacle-count signature identifying the floorplan (checked mechanically; colliding kitchens with the same binding are merged, with different bindings excluded); the ~30-row table is this benchmark's natural size and routing over hundreds of rows is not tested. Only Qwen3-32B; the reader's ability to execute a run-time probe or route a table may differ by backbone. W+/W- contexts are per game and uncached across games, the most expensive cells. The 200 held-out train games may differ in difficulty from valid_seen (stratum analysis). Same-kitchen hit rate below .8 would force a stronger key before any confirmatory cell.
Addresses gap: G2 (retriever vs fixed/static artifact never isolated): the residual of scene-keyed retrieval over the best static arm (static3 and its compiled augmentations from the same bank) is measured under a planted binding with the feedback regime manipulated on the same games, and the binding-created part is separated from the natural +17.2 by the within-game swap penalty; G3 (no whole-bank arm): the whole bank is run with the binding's presence randomised within game; cross-axis G6/G10 (retrieval vs knowledge never separated; relatedness threshold unmeasured) are attacked by making the binding's testability, not its presence, the manipulated variable, and by the oracle-key and oracle-name arms that bound what any lookup can add.
Not a restatement of: Prior-result bullet 'unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': this idea plants scene bindings and predicts that the retrieval residual over the best static arm is the natural +17.2 plus a binding-created term that exists only when the environment gives no probe and only against a static artifact that names a test instead of enumerating; a 60-token rule removes the term under the testable regime and an observation-keyed table removes it under the untestable one. Digest card arxiv:2605.22219 (SGR-Bench: failures come from the wrong site-specific state; whether stored procedures or prior trajectories would fix it is untested): this idea builds the stored procedures (table and rule) and the trajectory retrieval, and claims that which of them is needed is decided by whether the wrong state is detectable before committing, a property it manipulates on the same games rather than names.
Changes made: P1: the stale-playbook loss under untestable is now a construction check (reported, not scored); the gate is S3 (per-game oracle names) vs S0, which measures compliance and can fail. P2: kept open; restated as swap penalties, TOST margin set above the +-8 half-width, type-agnostic clause (T0) added, and the self-recovery outcome named as a result rather than a design failure. P3 (headline): estimand changed to D(R3, untestable) with S1's inertness stated as construction; the retriever is estimated separately by a pre-registered same-kitchen hit rate and the R3o oracle-key arm, so a null is attributable; stated why P3 is not implied by P1. P4: margin above the half-width by doubling the swapped cell (complementary assignments, 528 pairs, floor +-8); permuted-table placebo cut as forced; raw R3 - S2 stated against the measured +17.2 natural residual and the manipulation that keeps the binding from adding to it named (enumeration); T1 clause added. P5 (seen-unseen gap) removed and all unseen cells cut; 'Not a restatement of' rewritten around the regime x artifact interaction. P6 (whole bank): W+/W- with the same-kitchen item's presence randomised within game, paired, sizes and floor stated. P7 -> P5 (cost): threshold moved above the mechanical step count; an upper bound (post-probe flailing) and an unswapped over-testing clause added so the estimand can come out against the hypothesis. Design: untestable regime made one-shot (silent commit) because an undetectable-but-reversible failure is probe-able by redundancy and would let a 30-token rule bypass the binding; baseline changed to static3 (best measured) with type-agnostic playbook arms retained as controls; goal-keyed k3 and k0 at q = .5 cut; arithmetic 17,036 episodes, ~11.5 h on two A100s plus one day of engineering. Short Hypothesis: the contradiction between 'residual over the best compiled artifact' and 'the table matches the query' resolved: the residual over the best static arm is the natural residual once the artifact enumerates the binding; the binding-created term appears only against a non-enumerating artifact under the untestable regime. The central claim was not softened: it still predicts a regime x artifact interaction with both halves scored on the same games, and the one-shot regime makes the risky half harder to pass, not easier.
